extracted.intended_audience: readers, distributors, and republishers of Project Gutenberg eBooks; general readers of the eBook
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal requirements for using, copying, converting, distributing, or charging for Project Gutenberg electronic works (plus a literary text example: Jerome K. Jerome's humorous essays). Focus is on complying with the Project Gutenberg License and associated trademark rules when redistributing or republishing the eBook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader expectations for books (Preface)
rubrics_metrics.description: What readers ask nowadays in a book is that it should improve, instruct, and elevate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author states this as the contemporary expectation and contrasts his book as not meeting those aims; useful as a meta-criterion of what some audiences expect from literature, but the author explicitly disclaims that his work will not 'elevate' and offers it as light diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent display of the Project Gutenberg license sentence (1.E.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any copy of a Project Gutenberg work (or any work associated with the phrase 'Project Gutenberg') is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied or distributed, the specific license sentence in paragraph 1.E.1 must appear prominently with active links or immediate access to the full license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exact sentence (quoted in the license) must be shown prominently whenever the work is made available; failure to display that sentence breaches the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the 'Project Gutenberg' trademark requires agreement (1.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Project Gutenberg' trademark may only be used on or associated with an electronic work by people who agree to be bound by the license terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may do some things with most works without full compliance (see 1.C), but if you keep Project Gutenberg branding you must comply with the full license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted copying of public-domain texts if Project Gutenberg references removed (1.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual work is unprotected by U.S. copyright law and you are located in the United States, you may copy, distribute, perform, display or create derivative works as long as all references to Project Gutenberg are removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation hopes distributors will keep the Project Gutenberg name, but legally you may remove references and then redistribute freely within the U.S.; different rules apply if the work is posted with permission of a copyright holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not unlink, detach, or remove the full Project Gutenberg License from distributed copies (1.E.4 & 1.E.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distributors must not remove or detach the full Project Gutenberg License terms from the work or any files containing part of the work, and must prominently display the 1.E.1 sentence with active links whenever distributing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining the license text with distributed files (and the prominent sentence) is a strict requirement unless you have removed all references to Project Gutenberg per 1.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format conversion and requirement to provide original 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' on request (1.E.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may convert and distribute the work in many formats, but if you provide copies in formats other than the official 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' you must, at no additional cost, provide a means to obtain the original format upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any alternate format must include the full Project Gutenberg License; you must provide the original ASCII (or official original format) copy or a means to export it at no extra cost to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: No charging fees except when complying with charging rules (1.E.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access, viewing, displaying, performing, copying or distributing Project Gutenberg works unless you comply with paragraphs 1.E.8 or 1.E.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free distribution is the default; charging requires strict compliance (see detailed charging rules in 1.E.8) or written permission (1.E.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements if charging for copies or access (royalty, refunds, compliance) (1.E.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you charge a fee for copies/access/distribution you must: pay a 20% royalty of gross profits to the Project Gutenberg trademark owner (to be donated to the Foundation), provide full refunds on written request within 30 days to users who do not accept the license terms, provide refunds/replacements for defects reported within 90 days, and comply with all other terms of the agreement for free distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royalty payments: 20% of gross profits, paid within 60 days following periodic tax return dates; refunds must be offered and clearly handled; must comply with all license terms even when charging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate charging arrangements require written permission (1.E.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to charge or distribute Project Gutenberg works on terms different from those in the license, you must obtain written permission from the Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation (the trademark manager).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information and specific procedures for obtaining permission are provided in the license (Section 3).
